# What the stores let Agentship do

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-skill-references.ts from the adapters and the error catalog. Do not edit by hand. -->

This is the real coverage table of both adapters. Use it to answer "can you do X?" honestly
before promising anything, and to know in advance which parts of a release will need the user.

| Operation | Id | Apple | Google |
|---|---|---|---|
| Prove the stored credentials work | `checkAuth` | auto | auto |
| List the apps the credentials can see | `listApps` | auto | unsupported |
| Read the full state of one app | `getAppState` | auto | auto |
| List in-app products and subscriptions | `listProducts` | auto | auto |
| Read one product completely: prices per territory, offers, availability | `getProductState` | auto | auto |
| Read the state of a review submission | `getSubmissionStatus` | auto | auto |
| Compile and sign the app on this machine | `buildArtifact` | auto | auto |
| Create or reuse the editable store version | `ensureVersion` | auto | unsupported |
| Write listing text (name, description, keywords, what is new) | `setMetadata` | needs_approval | needs_approval |
| Upload and prune store images | `syncScreenshots` | needs_approval | needs_approval |
| Upload a build (.ipa / .aab) | `uploadBuild` | auto | auto |
| Release a build to a tester group or track | `distributeToTesters` | needs_approval | needs_approval |
| Create tester groups and manage members | `manageTesterGroups` | auto | auto |
| Set the price of the app | `setPricing` | needs_approval | agent_browser |
| Submit a version for review | `submitForReview` | needs_approval | needs_approval |
| Control phased release / staged rollout | `setPhasedRelease` | needs_approval | needs_approval |
| Release an approved version that the store is holding | `releaseVersion` | agent_browser | agent_browser |
| Create an in-app product or subscription | `createProduct` | needs_approval | needs_approval |
| Change a product’s name, period or localizations | `updateProduct` | needs_approval | needs_approval |
| Set a product’s price in each territory | `setProductPricing` | needs_approval | needs_approval |
| Create introductory or promotional offers | `setProductOffers` | needs_approval | needs_approval |
| Create the app record itself | `createApp` | agent_browser | agent_browser |
| Perform the very first release of an app | `firstRelease` | unsupported | agent_browser |
| Declare Apple App Privacy labels | `privacyLabels` | agent_browser | unsupported |
| Declare the Google Play Data Safety form | `dataSafety` | unsupported | needs_approval |
| Answer the content rating questionnaire | `contentRating` | needs_approval | agent_browser |
| Set up the pricing model of the app | `appPricing` | needs_approval | agent_browser |
| Choose the countries the app is available in | `appAvailability` | needs_approval | agent_browser |
| Answer the app content declarations | `appContentDeclarations` | unsupported | agent_browser |
| Configure Play App Signing | `playAppSigning` | unsupported | agent_browser |
| Reply to the review team | `resolutionCenter` | agent_browser | unsupported |
| Read a detailed review status | `reviewStatus` | unsupported | unsupported |
| Accept agreements and set up tax and banking | `agreementsTaxBanking` | human_only | human_only |

## What each classification means for you

- **auto** — Agentship does it; nothing to ask.
- **needs_approval** — Agentship can do it, but a human must approve the exact content first.
- **agent_browser** — No API. Agentship emits structured console instructions; an agent with a browser may follow them after showing the user what it will submit.
- **human_only** — No API, and a human must do it personally (identity, tax, banking, agreements, 2FA).
- **needs_input** — A value is missing before anything can happen.
- **unsupported** — Agentship will not do it by any means. Tell the user to do it in the console.

The classification in a plan can be stricter than this table: pricing, privacy declarations,
review submissions, destructive changes and anything reaching production are always
`needs_approval`, even where the store would allow Agentship to act alone.

## Console-only work known before any plan

### App Store Connect
- **Enrol in the Apple Developer Program** (`apple:developer-enrollment`, human_only) — Enrolment is a paid legal agreement between Apple and a verified individual or organisation. There is no API for it, and Apple verifies identity out of band (D-U-N-S number for an organisation, government ID for an individual). Console: https://developer.apple.com/programs/enroll/
- **Accept agreements and complete tax and banking details** (`apple:agreements-tax-banking`, human_only) — Apple requires the Account Holder to accept the Paid Applications agreement and to supply tax and banking information in person. None of it is exposed by the App Store Connect API. Console: https://appstoreconnect.apple.com/agreements
- **Create the App Store Connect API key** (`apple:api-key`, human_only) — API keys are issued in App Store Connect by a user with the Admin or Account Holder role. There is no API that creates an API key — that would be a bootstrap Apple does not offer. Console: https://appstoreconnect.apple.com/access/integrations/api
- **Create the app record in App Store Connect** (`apple:create-app-record`, agent_browser) — The App Store Connect API manages apps that already exist; it has no endpoint that creates one. The app record, its bundle ID and its SKU are created in the console. Console: https://appstoreconnect.apple.com/apps
- **Declare App Privacy data use** (`apple:app-privacy`, agent_browser) — App Privacy answers are not in the public App Store Connect API — verified against the 4.4.1 OpenAPI specification, which has no data-use resource — and they are a legal declaration about what the app really does. Console: https://appstoreconnect.apple.com/apps

### Google Play
- **Complete the developer account, identity verification and payments profile** (`google:account-and-payments`, human_only) — The one-time registration fee, identity verification and the payments profile are handled in Play Console by the account owner. Google exposes no API for any of them. Console: https://play.google.com/console/developers
- **Run the closed test a new personal account needs before production** (`google:closed-testing-requirement`, human_only) — Google requires a personal developer account created after 13 November 2023 to run a closed test with at least 12 testers who opted in, continuously for 14 days, and then to apply for production access. It is an account-level policy gate with no API. Console: https://play.google.com/console
- **Create the app in Play Console** (`google:create-app`, agent_browser) — The Google Play Developer API operates on apps that already exist. Creating the app, and choosing its package name, is only possible in Play Console. Console: https://play.google.com/console
- **Publish the first release from Play Console** (`google:first-release`, agent_browser) — Google requires a new app to reach its first release through the console. Until an app has been published once, API uploads to a track are rejected. Console: https://play.google.com/console
- **Complete the IARC content rating questionnaire** (`google:content-rating`, agent_browser) — Content ratings are issued by IARC, not by Google, through a questionnaire the developer answers under their own name. There is no API, and the answers are a declaration about the app's content. Console: https://play.google.com/console
- **Complete the App content declarations** (`google:app-content`, agent_browser) — Target audience, ads, news, government apps, financial features, health and the data safety review are answered in Play Console. Only the Data Safety form itself has an API (`applications.dataSafety`); the surrounding declarations do not. Console: https://play.google.com/console
- **Set the app price and the countries it is available in** (`google:pricing-and-countries`, agent_browser) — The Play Developer API prices in-app products, not the app itself. The app price, its free/paid status and its country availability are console-only. Console: https://play.google.com/console

## Two limits worth telling the user early

- A new personal Google Play account must run a closed test with at least 12 testers for 14
  continuous days before it can publish to production. It cannot be bypassed; plan for it.
- Apple issues the App Store Connect `.p8` key file exactly once. If it is lost, the key has
  to be revoked and a new one generated.
